challenges.name: topics-partitions-keys-quiz
challenges.title: Read the first event streams
challenges.description: Three statements about what Rice Rocket saw after the api started writing order events to Kafka. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: Kafka keeps an order per partition, not per topic. Ask which partition each event of order o-1842 went to when the events had no key.
The key decides the partition. How many distinct keys does a restaurant chain with hundreds of orders produce, and how many partitions can those keys land in?
The default partitioner takes the key's hash modulo the partition count. What happens to that result when the count changes from 12 to 24?

questions.explanation: False. Kafka orders messages within one partition only. Without a key the producer spread o-1842's four events over partitions 3, 0, 5 and 1, and a consumer group reads partitions independently, so OrderDelivered on partition 1 can be processed before CourierAssigned on partition 5. Keying every event by its order id puts all of an order's events in one partition, in produce order. The misconception is that a topic is one ordered queue.

questions.question:
After keying events by `restaurantId`, the lunch rush looked like this (one consumer per partition):

```text
$ kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group courier-matcher
GROUP            TOPIC      PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
courier-matcher  orders.v1  0          88412           88420           8
courier-matcher  orders.v1  4          301877          320102          18225
courier-matcher  orders.v1  7          91033           91040           7
... (9 more partitions with a lag under 10)
```

Statement: "Every order of the big chain shares one key, so they all hash to partition 4 and one consumer does most of the work; keying by order id spreads the chain's orders and still keeps each order's events in order."
questions.explanation: True. One key always maps to the same partition, so a key with most of the traffic makes a hot partition, and adding consumers does not help: a partition is read by one consumer of the group. Order ids are many and roughly uniform, so they spread over all partitions, and each order's events still share one key. The misconception is that keying by a coarse entity (restaurant, city) is safer; it is only needed when events of different orders must be ordered relative to each other.

questions.question:
The team plans to double the partitions of the topic while orders keep flowing:

```text
$ kafka-topics --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --alter --topic orders.v1 --partitions 24
$ kafka-topics --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --topic orders.v1 | head -1
Topic: orders.v1  PartitionCount: 24  ReplicationFactor: 3  Configs: min.insync.replicas=2
```

Statement: "After the change many order ids map to a different partition, so an order placed before the change can have its later events in a new partition and, for a while, be read out of order."
questions.explanation: True. The default partitioner computes the key's murmur2 hash modulo the partition count, so most keys move when the count goes from 12 to 24. Events already written stay where they are; the next events of the same order go to the new partition, and a consumer of that partition can process them before the old partition's consumer has caught up. Kafka can add partitions but never removes them. Pick the count up front, with room to grow, or switch over during a quiet window.

challenges.name: order-events-producer
challenges.title: Key the order events
challenges.description: The api's first producer sent order events without a key, and OrderDelivered sometimes reached consumers before CourierAssigned; keying by restaurant then made one partition carry the lunch rush of a big chain. The editor holds `main.ts`: the topic spec `ORDERS_TOPIC` and `toMessage(event)` with their key blocks missing, each marked by a `// [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that: `orders.v1` has 12 partitions, replication factor 3 and `min.insync.replicas` 2; every event of one order lands in one partition, in the order it was produced; the chain's orders do not pile onto one partition; and each record carries the headers `event-type` and `schema-version` ("1"). Run produces a lunch rush into an in-memory broker that uses Kafka's default partitioner (murmur2 of the key).
hints: Ask what must stay in order: the events of one order, or the events of one restaurant? The key decides the partition, and only a partition is ordered.
Look at the key returned by `toMessage`, the `headers` object of the message, and `numPartitions`, `replicationFactor` and `configEntries` of the topic spec.

Courier GPS pings, where each courier's pings must stay in order and couriers are many: `const COURIERS_TOPIC = { topic: "couriers.v1", numPartitions: 6, replicationFactor: 3, configEntries: [{ name: "min.insync.replicas", value: "2" }] }` and `const key = ping.courierId;` with `headers = { "event-type": "CourierPing", "schema-version": "2" }`.

tests.name: orders.v1 has 12 partitions, replication factor 3 and min.insync.replicas 2
Every event of one order lands in one partition
A delivered order replays in the order it was produced
The chain's lunch rush (60% of orders) does not pile onto one partition
A cancelled order replays in order, and records carry the type and version headers
